title: Short Stuff: Jack O'Lanterns and Sleepy Hollow
summary: Short Stuff episode for Halloween that covers two linked topics. First, the Irish legend of Stingy Jack, the drinking companion who tricked the devil into a coin and then into a tree, and who was left wandering with a burning coal in a carved turnip, giving rise to the Jack-o'-lantern (with the hosts noting the turnip, potato, beet, and American pumpkin variations). Second, Washington Irving's "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow," covering the Headless Horseman, Ichabod Crane, the real Sleepy Hollow in Westchester County, New York, real local landmarks Irving wove in, the possible real Colonel Ichabod Crane, and the Hessian mercenary who lost his head to a cannonball at the Battle of White Plains in 1776, plus influences like the Grimm Brothers, Sir Walter Scott's "The Chase," and Gottfried Bürger's "The Wild Huntsman."

segments.title: Opening banter and the Stingy Jack legend
segments.summary: The hosts open the Halloween-themed short episode and recount the Irish legend of Stingy Jack, who tricked the devil into becoming a coin and later into climbing a tree, then was refused entry to both heaven and hell and wandered with a burning coal in a carved turnip, which became the Jack-o'-lantern.

segments.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow and the Headless Horseman
segments.summary: The hosts describe Washington Irving's story set in Sleepy Hollow, New York, where schoolmaster Ichabod Crane is rebuffed by Katrina van Tassel and chased by the Headless Horseman, who throws a pumpkin that knocks Crane off his horse. Crane is never heard from again.

segments.title: Real history and folklore behind the story
segments.summary: The hosts discuss real places Irving used, a possible real Colonel Ichabod Crane, the Hessian mercenary who lost his head to a cannonball at the Battle of White Plains in 1776, and earlier headless horseman tales from the Grimm Brothers, Sir Walter Scott's The Chase, and Gottfried Bürger's The Wild Huntsman.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts recommend listeners read Irving's story and close the episode with a plug for the show.
